terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A glazed display cart on four wheels. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches -- the cover, jar and bag roll are dressing -- so there are no sockets. Sidewalk fruit vendors, temple fairs, office soi corners. A dented stainless frame, glass running with condensation, pineapple, mango and watermelon banked on shaved ice, a jar of bamboo skewers, a folded canvas cover on the rail, a roll of bags.

reasoning: ONE angle-steel frame merge -- four posts, sixteen rails, two back mullions, the ice tray, the chassis deck, the axle spine, four castor forks, the push handle, the bag-roll hangers, five folds of canvas with their rounded fold edges and seventeen bamboo skewers; ONE glazing component of four transparent panes; ONE bed component of the ice bank, its chips and crest, sixteen pineapple slices, eight mango slices, seven watermelon wedges with rind and pith, the skewer jar and the bag roll; ONE InstancedMesh of four castors: FOUR draw calls of 4.

Three materials of the four allowed: steel (vertex colours carry stainless, the dark axles and castor forks, and the canvas), real TRANSPARENT glass at opacity 0.26 both-sided, and a wet material for ice, fruit, jar and bag roll -- the glazing is a separate render state that cannot share with the opaque parts.
One repetition system: four castors off one two-cylinder geometry, each a named pivot.
Action readiness: four hinge pivots on the castors, one box collider on the root, zero sockets, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the glazed case with the banked ice and three fruit colours inside, on wheels; the glass has to be real transparency or the fruit is invisible and the prop is a steel box.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The back face carries two mid mullions: the plate shows two steel verticals above the ice line and both are occluded below it, which places them on the far face rather than on the front pane, and the front pane is left clear.

The skewer jar is built on the OPAQUE wet material rather than the glazing. At the 0.26 opacity the panes need, a jam-jar-sized cylinder renders as nothing at all, and the plate's jar is packed solid with sticks.

Albedo is authored for this harness key light, not for the eye: an up-facing slice renders at roughly 1.05x its albedo plus a 60-count ambient, and the plate is lit flat and shadowless, so the plate's #d8bd69 pineapple is carried as #c79412 and lands at #cfbf7c behind the pane against the plate's measured #d8bd69.

The bag roll length is read off the plate as running along the cart depth on the +X side; its stand-off from the side face is the one dimension the single view cannot fix, and it is set so the bbox closes at the declared 1.43.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.43 x 1.50 x 0.76 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 4 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: A 1.28 x 0.73 m glazed case from 0.23 to 1.30 m on a chassis over four r 0.105 castors at +-0.48, +-0.26; a stainless tray at 0.85 carrying an ice bank that ramps from 0.955 at the front lip to 1.262 at the back crest, two ranks of pineapple, mango and watermelon lying on it; a folded canvas 1.04 x 0.15 on the back half of the top rail; a jar of skewers on the back-left corner to 1.52; a bag roll r 0.056 x 0.35 on the +X hangers with a sheet hanging off it; a push handle over the +X rail.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: Solved off the PLATE, not estimated. Picking the three case bottom corners in the reference -- front-left (175,703), front-right (620,870), back-right (838,762) px -- gives a width edge of (445,167) and a depth edge of (218,-108), so tan(t)sin(p)=167/445=0.375 and sin(p)/tan(t)=108/218=0.495: elevation 25.5 deg, yaw 41.0 deg. Unforeshortened the case is 590 x 489 x 332 world-px inside a total 685 from the castor contact to the skewer tips, i.e. w/H 0.861, d/H 0.485, case 0.714 H, castors and chassis 0.153 H, jar and cover 0.133 H. At the declared h 1.50 that is a case 1.28 x 0.73 from y 0.23 to 1.30, a mid rail and tray at 0.85, castors r 0.105 at +-0.48, +-0.26, and the bag roll on the +X side carrying the bbox to 1.43 wide. Built 1.416 x 1.541 x 0.742. The Meshy proxy independently agrees on width (bbox w/H 0.881) and case height (0.70 H) and reads 36 per cent deep (d/H 0.659), which is what a single-view reconstruction does to depth; the plate solve governs. The first build declared 1.70 x 1.50 x 0.75, which made the case w/h 1.73 against the plate 1.21 and is why it read long and low.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bbox w/H 0.881, d/H 0.659, H 1.902 m normalised. Per height band at the 1-99 percentile the case body alone is w/H 0.79 and d/H 0.60, and the occupancy is castors 0-0.19 H, case 0.19-0.93 H, cover to 0.97 H. It agrees with the plate solve on width and on case height and disagrees on depth by 36 per cent, which is the known single-view depth inflation, so the plate solve governs the depth and the proxy corroborates the stations.

componentTree.name: Ice bed and cut fruit

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: The bank is a solid profile swept along x carrying a jittered 16x9 height grid as its surface -- front lip z +0.31 at 0.955, back crest z -0.31 at 1.262, both dropping to the tray at 0.838 -- with loose chips on it, a crumbled front lip and a heaped crest. Two ranks of fruit lie on it at z 0.26 and 0.17: pineapple x -0.58 to -0.14, mango -0.10 to 0.13, watermelon 0.25 to 0.50.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Every fruit piece is rotated on three axes and sunk into the bank; the chips are individually rotated; the bank meets the tray as an opposed butt. Nothing co-facing.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components and one repetition system: 4 of 4.

materials.note: steel, glass and wet: 3 of the 4 allowed, the glass a separate render state by the registry notes.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,796 of 4,000: the frame and its dressing, four panes, the ice bank with thirty-one fruit pieces and fifty-six chips, and a two-cylinder castor instanced four times.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes for the frame, tray, deck, cover, panes, ice chips and pineapple; a swept profile for the ice bank and for each watermelon wedge with its rind and pith; scaled spheres for the mango slices; cylinders for the fold edges, jar, skewers, bag roll and castors.
One InstancedMesh: four wheels, each a named pivot with its instance index on sculptRuntime.pivots.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. Two 256 px canvases after construction -- frame grime and pane meltwater -- 0.5 MB of texture VRAM, and the factory builds in 82 ms.

risks.description: Four transparent panes in one mesh sort as one; the far pane can draw over the near one at some angles.
risks.mitigation: Opacity 0.26 and a pale green cast make the order invisible at prop distance; depthWrite stays on.

risks.description: The lower half of the case is empty now that the ice sits on a tray at mid height, so the backdrop is visible through two panes inside the silhouette.
risks.mitigation: The pane composites that region at luma 131 over the backdrop 58 -- the plate's own measured 127 -- well clear of the hole gate's grey band.

risks.description: The Meshy proxy reads d/H 0.659 against the plate solve's 0.485.
risks.mitigation: Single-view reconstructions inflate depth; the projective solve off three picked corners governs, and the proxy corroborates width and case height to within 3 per cent.
